title: A short stage at a large context, where the cache lifetime decides the break-even
brief: Today is {{TODAY}}. Harness: Claude Code desktop app. The harness reports this session's model as claude-sonnet-5-5 at effort medium.
The session usage tool reports tokensUsed 400,000, contextWindow 1,000,000 and autoCompactsAtPercent 97. This session has not been compacted.
A fresh session in this harness and project starts at 86,450 tokens (measured: the usage tool's total less its Messages category).

Next stage: a bug fix inside one module, with its test suite as the oracle. The module does not touch authentication, payments, storage formats or a public interface. Plan estimate: 13 turns, each reading about 2,000 tokens of tool output and writing about 1,000 tokens (measured on the last three fixes in this module).
A fresh session would read 13,550 tokens: the handoff and the module.
A handoff for this stage would be about 80 lines.
If the stage goes to a fresh session, the operator starts it from a card and this session ends; nobody coordinates.
Everything this session knows that the next stage needs is already written in files on disk.
No cache-miss measurement exists, and no review pauses are expected during the stage.
The usage report shows every cache write in this session as a 1-hour write.
The stage writes files and commits locally; nothing leaves the machine.

alternatives.why: the harness writes 5-minute entries: every write is cheaper, T* falls from 14.2 to 9.2 turns, T 13 is past it and fresh is cheaper by more than the band
the same inputs under formula 2026-11-10, which priced every write at the 5-minute figure: the verdict the formula of that date would have given

notes: Added in Stage O6 (2026-11-10) with formula 2026-11-11, the first scenario under it. Figures captured from the calculator and derived by hand first: T* = (H x p_out + (B + R) x p_cw) / ((C0 - B - R) x p_cr) = (2,500 x 10e-6 + 100,000 x 4e-6) / (300,000 x 0.1e-6) = 0.425 / 0.03 = 14.17 turns at the 1-hour write price, and (0.025 + 0.25) / 0.03 = 9.17 at the 5-minute one.

T 13 lies between the two, so the lifetime alone decides: under 1h the short path settles step A as continue; under 5m both sides are computed and fresh is cheaper by more than the band. The 1-hour figure comes from two facts in the brief: the harness (step 7 names the Claude Code desktop app's 1-hour writes) and the usage report, which step 1.1 reads first.
To 0: the operator starts any fresh session from a card and this session ends (step 1.2). No coordinator. The block must state To 0, no coordinator and ttl 1h (rubric section 2).
Not a guardrail 1 case: T 13 is not under 10 turns. The stage is matrix row 2 (Sonnet, medium), the class this session already runs.
